PullRequest.Title: resourceTree: keep a folder's own entry when its last child is deleted
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #348975

This carries over #348976 by @rezacr588, because pull requests from forks can't be merged right now. Their commit is included unchanged, and the squash commit credits them as co-author. The second commit only extends the test.

**Before:** Removing the last file inside a folder from a resource tree also removed the folder's own entry, if it had one. A folder has its own entry when it is also a changed item, for example when a tracked file `config` is replaced by a folder `config/` with new files in it. Resource trees hold the folder structure behind the tree views in Source Control, the multi diff editor's file list and the Changes view.

**After:** The folder and its entry stay. Empty folders without an entry of their own are still removed, as before.

Nothing changes for users today: those views rebuild their trees on every update instead of removing entries one at a time. The fix stops any future code that removes entries from silently losing them.

This stays a draft until the contributor signs the CLA on #348976.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- **Root cause:** `ResourceTree._delete()` pruned an intermediate node as soon as `childrenCount === 0`, without checking whether the node has its own `element`. `add()` supports such nodes, and the existing `folders with data` test treats them as valid.
- **Fix** (commit by @rezacr588): only prune nodes whose `element` is `undefined`.
- **Test** (second commit): the regression test now also checks that empty folders without an element are still pruned up to the first folder that has one, and that deleting a file in another folder still removes that folder once it is empty. It asserts the whole tree in one snapshot, and fails when the fix is reverted.
- **Why nothing is affected today:** no production code calls `ResourceTree.delete()`. The Source Control view stopped calling it in #197349; each resource group now discards its tree on every change and rebuilds it with `add()`. The multi diff editor's file list, the Changes view, the Graph view and the artifacts view also build fresh trees. I checked this in Code OSS with logpoints: deleting `config/settings.json` in a repository where the tracked file `config` had been replaced by that folder only rebuilt trees and never called `delete()`. The Source Control tree and the multi diff file list showed the same rows with and without the fix.
- **Unchanged:** deleting a folder that has both an element and children still removes the whole subtree.

**Validation**

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/base/test/common/resourceTree.test.ts`: 5 passing. The new test fails when the fix is reverted.
- `./scripts/test.sh` with the ResourceTree, SCM (`scmStructuralDiff`, `scmRepositoryVisibility`), multi diff editor (`multiDiffEditorWithFileList`, `actions`, `multiDiffEditorConfiguration`) and Changes view (`changesViewRenderer`) suites: 67 passing.
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/base/test/common/resourceTree.test.ts`: no issues.

</details>

Scenarios.Scenario: Delete a resource's last descendant while retaining an ancestor with its own element; also delete ordinary leaves, missing paths, or whole subtrees.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ResourceTree.delete synchronously computes a relative path, traverses path segments, removes the target, and unwinds ancestor pruning. The added element check is a plain field read on that existing unwind path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Path length/depth controls deletion work. Retained nodes correspond to explicitly added, still-live elements and their ancestor paths, not deletion history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous traversal per call; no tasks, promises, subprocesses, or concurrent work introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No external cache or negative-cache state. Map lookups and size checks remain in-memory; absent paths terminate early. Explicit deletion and clear still remove retained elements.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete ResourceTree implementation, PathIterator, URI-relative-path implementation, and changed test establish the mechanism directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings measured; additional field checks are bounded by the existing traversal depth.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Previously pruning could discard a still-live ancestor element; now that element and required ancestors remain until explicitly removed. This is required ownership, not unbounded retention, and does not change traversal complexity.

Scenarios.Scenario: Update Source Control resource groups after files are removed or changed.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing extension-host batching delivers resource splices; the main thread applies them and invalidates each affected group's tree. A later resourceTree getter synchronously rebuilds the group using add before rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send grouped SCMRawResourceSplices from extension host to main thread.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call for all nonempty updated-group snapshots collected by the existing 100 ms debounce, per source-control instance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical grouped, debounced IPC and repository barrier; group splice already discarded its cached tree and rebuilding already used add rather than delete.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resource updates must arrive and pass the existing repository barrier before main-thread group updates and subsequent tree rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One batched update can contain several groups and slices. Rebuilding scales with the resources and path depths in an accessed group, not with one IPC per resource.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Extension-host updates are debounced and grouped. Main-thread splice application and each lazy rebuild are synchronous; the existing repository barrier can delay update application.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Group tree is lazy and reused on warm reads; splice invalidates it. The next read builds a fresh tree. Neither invalidation nor cache lifetime changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected extension-host batching, main-thread splice entry point and application, and resourceTree getter/invalidation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Group sizes and provider timings vary, but none of those costs are increased by this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: this production workflow never reaches the changed deletion condition. Existing IPC, allocations, and rebuilding are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build or refresh multi-diff file lists and the Changes view folder hierarchy.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing in-memory items are sorted/grouped and converted into renderable tree elements. Both workflows construct fresh ResourceTree instances and populate them with add/getNode rather than delete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of existing file/diff items, distinct paths after grouping, and path depths; duplicate multi-diff paths share tree nodes while preserving their items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous local construction and traversal; no new async work or boundary calls on these tree-building paths.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: These builders create fresh temporary trees per invocation; duplicate paths are grouped by existing maps/node elements. No new cache, invalidation, or retained history is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected getFileListElements, sortMultiDiffEditorFileListItems, and buildTreeChildren.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large lists can have existing sorting/construction costs, but the changed method is not called by these builders.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: all production tree-building work in these paths is unchanged, and richer retained state is not introduced into their fresh trees by the new condition.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand Source Control history changes or artifact folders.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing provider requests finish before a fresh resource tree is populated with all returned changes/artifacts. Descendant-folder expansion reads existing node children.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request a history item's changes and, for incoming/outgoing special cases, resolve a common ancestor through the extension-host proxy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One changes request per history-item children request, optionally preceded by one ancestor request; all returned changes are inserted locally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same provider requests, ordering, and fresh add-only tree construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Ancestor resolution, when necessary, precedes the changes request; the changes response precedes tree construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request artifact groups for a repository or all artifacts in an expanded group.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One groups request per repository children request; one artifacts request per group children request, not per artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same provider calls and fresh add-only ResourceTree population.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider response is awaited before constructing returned children and an optional folder tree.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Requests are per expanded history item or artifact group, with local tree construction proportional to returned resources/path depths; not one provider request per resource.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each children request awaits its provider call, with conditional history ancestor lookup sequentially before changes. Independent expansions retain their existing scheduling; the diff introduces no concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The inspected data-source methods build fresh trees from provider results; any provider-side caching remains outside and unchanged. Existing folder nodes serve descendant expansion without a new provider call.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged request placement/cardinality and add-only construction, based on data-source methods and extension-host proxy implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider implementations may perform additional filesystem/network/subprocess work, whose duration and internal caching were not measured; invocation count and scheduling do not change.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: neither workflow calls the changed deletion path, and the diff adds or moves no provider boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the newly added ResourceTree deletion regression test.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test constructs three entries, performs two synchronous deletions, then snapshots the remaining nodes and collects elements for one assertion.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed tree with three inserted elements and a few path segments; describeNodes visits only the small surviving tree.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous unit-test operations; no new parallel activity.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Test-local objects become unreachable after completion; no long-lived cache is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete new test and helper were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured test duration, but input size is fixed and tiny.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression. Recursive array construction is test-only and operates on a fixed tiny fixture.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the entire two-file inventory and both complete diffs against base b4f9b4b433225d57b7c7c9626abb70eb0b4d9db4. Traced deletion/pruning ownership, affected test work, and production tree consumers including grouped SCM IPC and history/artifact provider boundaries. The production change adds only an element-preservation guard during deletion; retained elements are live explicit entries, and current inspected product consumers rebuild trees instead of calling delete. No high-confidence performance regression or qualifying performance-regression fix was found. Static read-only review; no performance measurements.
